source.stem: A 9 V ideal source powers a 3 Ω resistor in series with two 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel. Determine total current and current in each branch, and state why neither branch sees 9 V.
source.decisive_work: Differentiate the voltage across a parallel block from the source voltage when a series drop exists.

shortest_valid_route: Identify the two common nodes for parallel resistors and the series element upstream
Reduce only the actual parallel branch block before the series element
Compute the source current and downstream node-pair voltage
Check branch currents sum to the series current and rule out full source voltage across the block
task.protected_decisive_work: Choose a mixed-series/parallel graph, distinguish branch voltage from source voltage, conserve junction current.
task.model_conditions: Steady DC, ideal 12 V source, ideal wires, ideal ohmic resistors at unchanged temperature, no unintended crossing connections.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Choose mixed series/parallel topology before applying any current formula

representation_translation.evidence: Map the connection graph to node-pair voltage, not drawing proximity

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Sequentially reduce the block and check conserved current through the junction

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Simple resistor arithmetic once topology is selected

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Parallel branches share their mutual node voltage, not necessarily the full source voltage
